verdict: Principal's headline profit nearly tripled to $632M, but most of the jump came from an $818M paper gain on a derivative tied to a business it has exited — the steadier operating business earned $482M, up 2%, while managing $785B of assets.

segments.name: Premiums and other considerations
segments.note: Premiums for retirement, pension and insurance products — up 24% versus a year ago.

segments.name: Fees and other revenues
segments.note: Fees for managing money and administering retirement plans and accounts.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the investments Principal holds against future policyholder payments — down 3% on lower variable investment income.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Running the company: staff, systems, commissions and administration.

otherDetail: An $818M gain in the fair value of a funds-withheld embedded derivative tied to an exited business, less $388M of net realized capital losses and $17M of losses on funds-withheld assets. Noncontrolling interests absorbed a $35M loss, which lifts the profit belonging to Principal's shareholders.

follow100.label: Other income (derivative gain, net of investment losses)

follow100Note: Other income added $10.66 per $100 of operating revenue (a derivative gain, partly offset by investment losses, plus the noncontrolling-interest effect), which is why the kept-as-profit row is larger than what was left after costs and tax alone. Cost of revenue is benefits, claims and settlement expenses plus policy-benefit remeasurement losses and dividends to policyholders. Rows are rounded to cents.

takeaways.title: A paper gain tripled headline profit
takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $632M versus $214M a year ago, driven by an $818M increase in the fair value of a derivative tied to a reinsurance deal for a business Principal has exited. It is a valuation swing, not cash from selling anything.

takeaways.title: The operating business grew slowly
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP operating earnings were $2.22 per share (+6%), or $2.49 excluding significant variances (+7%). Retirement & Income Solutions earned $298M before tax and Investment Management $168M; life insurance swung to a $32M profit from a $69M loss on better mortality experience.

takeaways.title: Cash went back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Principal returned $429M in the quarter — $250M of share buybacks and $179M of dividends — and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.85 per share for the fourth quarter.

oneTimers: $818M pre-tax gain from the change in fair value of the funds-withheld embedded derivative on an exited business — excluded from Principal's non-GAAP operating earnings.
A $277M pre-tax loss on the disposition of Principal's Chilean annuities business, also inside the exited-business results.

$388M of net realized capital losses (GAAP), versus gains of $86M a year ago — excluded from operating earnings, which is why non-GAAP net income excluding the exited business was $355M ($1.64 per share) even as GAAP EPS hit $2.91.
footerNote: Revenue here is premiums plus fees plus net investment income; GAAP total revenue was $4,616M including the items in Other income.
